Well, honestly, yes, it really has. I mean, I'm still dragging myself out of bed and going to work, mostly because I just feel this immense guilt about calling out and leaving my unit short-staffed. You know how it is in healthcare, if one nurse calls out, everyone else suffers, and I just can't bear the thought of my patients not getting the care they need because I couldn't get it together. It was humiliating, honestly, having her point it out, but I couldn't even defend myself because she was right. I'm just so distracted by this heaviness that I'm dropping the ball.

And it's not just work, either. Like I mentioned before about not texting my friends back... I'm really pulling away from everyone. My friends from the ward, my husband... I just don't have the bandwidth to engage with them. I'm neglecting the things that usually keep me steady and grounded. Even at home, the laundry is just piling up in the corner of the bedroom. It's been sitting there in this massive heap for two weeks, and every time I walk past it, I think, 'I really need to wash those,' but I just keep walking and get back on the couch. Cooking? Forget it. My husband has been ordering takeout almost every night because I can't even stomach the idea of standing in the kitchen and chopping vegetables or boiling water. It's just all too much. So, yeah, I guess I'm physically showing up to some things, but I'm definitely not functioning the way I need to be. It's just bleeding into every single part of my life right now.

Well, it's definitely the slowing down. I haven't been restless at all, just... incredibly sluggish. I know I mentioned feeling like I was walking through molasses a minute ago, but it really is exactly like that. Or maybe like I'm moving through thick, heavy syrup. It's the charting, too, which I know we just talked about, but it's not just that I'm missing things—it's that finishing the charting takes me so much longer than it ever used to. I'm just staring at the screen, and typing a simple sentence feels like this huge, monumental task. One of the other nurses actually asked me if I was feeling sick the other day because she was waiting on me to bring some supplies to room four and I was just moving at an absolute snail's pace. I just feel so physically bogged down, like gravity has been turned up all the way just for me. It's exhausting just trying to put one foot in front of the other, let alone trying to keep up with the normal pace of the day.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Honestly, eating has just become this massive chore. I mean, I know I should be eating regularly, I really do. Especially now, when I'm already feeling so drained and exhausted all the time, you'd think I'd want to fuel my body, right? As a nurse, I'm literally lecturing my patients all day about how important proper nutrition is for their energy levels and overall health, so the irony isn't lost on me. But... I just can't force myself to care about it right now. 

Most days, food just sounds completely unappealing. It really doesn't matter what it is. My husband will ask what I want for dinner, or he'll suggest ordering from that little Thai place I used to be obsessed with, and my stomach just kind of turns at the idea of it. The actual physical act of chewing and swallowing just feels like I'd be eating cardboard. Nothing sounds good, nothing tastes good. 

So what ends up happening is, I'll go into work, and because I'm already struggling so much to keep up with the pace of the clinic and everything takes me twice as long like I was just saying, I just completely skip my breaks. I'll be in the middle of charting or doing a dressing change, and I'll suddenly look up at the clock and realize it's halfway through my shift—like, one or two in the afternoon—and it'll dawn on me that the only thing I've put in my body all day is a cup of lukewarm coffee from the breakroom and maybe a couple of those dry saltine crackers from the patient supply closet. And even those crackers, I basically have to force them down with a huge gulp of water just to stop my stomach from growling while I'm trying to listen to someone's heart rate. I used to be so good about meal prepping on Sundays, packing these nice, balanced lunches in little containers for the whole week, but now... the appetite just isn't there at all. I'm basically just running on coffee and fumes.

Honestly, this is the hardest part for me to talk about. It really is. And it’s actually the whole reason I’m even here talking to you today, because... well, I haven't told anyone at work, obviously, and my husband knows I'm struggling with my energy, but I haven't been entirely truthful with him about how dark my head has gotten. 

I had a routine prenatal appointment recently—which, you know, being pregnant right now is supposed to be this incredibly joyous, exciting time where you're planning for the future, but I've just been feeling so empty and depleted instead. And at that appointment, my OB was just doing the standard check-in, asking how I was feeling, and I just completely broke down. Because what really scared me—what scared me enough to actually open my mouth and say something to her at that prenatal appointment—was that I’ve been having these thoughts lately like... I just wish I wouldn’t wake up. 

It’s not that I want to actively end my life. I really need to be clear about that. As a nurse, I know what suicidal ideation looks like, I know what it means to have a plan, and I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. I would never do anything to intentionally harm myself or the baby. But the exhaustion of just getting through a single day is so profound right now. I’ll go to bed at night, after dragging myself through a shift at the clinic and feeling like I'm moving through that heavy syrup we talked about, and I'll just lie there in the dark and think, "It would be so nice if I just stayed asleep." 

Like, if I just didn't have to open my eyes tomorrow and face the crushing weight of trying to function for another twenty-four hours. It just feels like slipping away in my sleep would be this huge relief, just a break from how hard everything is. And having a thought like that... especially now, when I'm supposed to be bringing a new life into the world... it absolutely terrified me. It made me feel sick to my stomach to realize my brain was even going there. That’s when I knew I couldn't just chalk this up to being tired from work or normal pregnancy fatigue anymore. I knew I had to tell the doctor, because having those thoughts of just wanting to disappear into sleep forever... it's just too scary to deal with by myself.
